text:
maya: heads-up: customers reporting JSON parse errors on SSE chunks. clients receive two back-to-back data frames that interleave and the JS parser chokes on the concatenated payload. repro on both node-fetch and browser SSE.
nina: any sample payloads or trace ids?
maya: trace=def456, trace=def459. payloads show partial utf8 boundary split in middle of object, ends up like '{\"choices\":[' + '\"text': 'hello'...' no comma between frames.
derek: is this at the runtime or proxy boundary? looks like chunk coalescing in our old http->sse transform.
suresh: could be our connection pool doing writev merges; when runtime flushes two small writes close together, proxy coalesces and drops the separator char if transform logic expects per-write boundaries.
zoe: console metric spike: stream.json_parse_errors up 0.2% in last 4h. panel: https://console/redwood/d/streaming?view=jsonparse. top-affected routes: /v1/chat/stream (public).
ops: immediate customer impact: some clients crash and re-open streams leading to duplicate completions and billing noise. Also poor UX.
nina: short-term mitigation: add client-side guidance doc: recommend tolerant parser or buffer until valid JSON object; but we need server-side fix.
derek: quick server fix options: 1) ensure we emit explicit delimiter between messages (\n\n or explicit boundary token) before any coalescing, 2) disable writev coalescing on the proxy lambda path, 3) force runtime to serialize full frame in single write.
suresh: disabling writev globally is heavy. forcing runtime might be easiest for new model adapters (we can batch writes). But we need a quick proxy-side toggle for canary.
zoe: telemetry ask: tag spans with chunk.coalesced=true/false and add counter stream.coalesced_writes. we can then correlate to json_parse_errors.
ops: propose config key streaming.coalesce_guard=true|false. default true (allow coalescing). Canary false for subset. If false, proxy will insert explicit \n\n delimiter between SSE data frames when conversion sees adjacent write boundaries.
maya: agree. also add metric stream.delimiter_inserts to see how often we trigger.
derek: for rollback safety, set deploy to 2% -> 10% -> 30% with automatic rollback on client error spike (>15% increase in 4xx/5xx).
nina: UX on console: add a heatmap for parse errors by SDK version so we can notify specific customers. Also add a note on recommended client resilience.
suresh: longer term: modify runtime SDKs to include a small header X-Redwood-Stream-Frame: id so proxies preserve boundaries safely. That also helps for resume behavior.
zoe: I'll add dashboard tiles: json_parse_errors (rate), coalesced_writes_by_route, delimiter_inserts, sdk_version_heatmap. Link will go into the canary playbook.
ops: I'll PR the proxy flag and test locally with simulated small writes. Deploy-bot: created rollout CH-10002, owner=ops, rollback_on=client_error_spike.
deploy-bot: rollout scheduled: 02:00 UTC canary start, evaluation window 30m.
maya: can someone own correlating billing delta? we need to ensure we don't double-charge while canary runs.
derek: I'll add a quick guard in the billing service to de-dupe completions if resume detected within 2s from same trace id. temporary until fix rolls out.
nina: good. I'll draft the customer note explaining buffer tolerant parsing and link to SDK examples.
suresh: I'll work on trace tagging change and frame-id header RFC.
zoe: created draft panels and will add alert: json_parse_errors >0.1% over 15m triggers pager to eng-platform-oncall.
ops: ack, PR queued.
maya: action summary: ops proxy flag canary, derek billing de-dupe guard, suresh runtime headers + trace tags, zoe dashboards + alerts, nina customer note. meet tomorrow 10:00 to review canary metrics.
nina: ack
derek: ack
